correctness.rationale: The homogeneous gradient gives exactly six points on the three axes, and a local unit-square completion yields six geometric A2 cusps with delta one. The coordinate-square map is an independent geometric integrality certificate: the Kummer square classes on smooth Hesse cubic E are independent by odd valuations at two distinct flexes; branch indices 2 over three flexes give genus four. A genus-two intermediate has the explicitly reconstructed equation r²=(t³/λ+t)²-1; its two involutions yield E and F, and the order-four character decomposition yields Jac(C)∼E×F³ over k. Both elliptic factors are smooth and have nonzero characteristic-three Hasse invariants. Unibranch residue-preserving cusps and isogeny give zeta equality. Verified by direct finite-field point enumeration over F3,F9,F27 for both λ in F3*, with independently computed elliptic traces. No finite test was used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The characteristic-three degeneration of a symmetric Fermat-descendant subfamily excluded by the source’s characteristic hypotheses has a sharp geometric change from smooth genus-ten sextics to six-cuspidal genus-four curves. Identifying an explicit elliptic four-factor isogeny and uniform ordinarity over every nonzero parameter, together with exact zeta-function factorization, determines the arithmetic rather than merely listing singularities. The two distinct F3 models are both ordinary pointless genus-four curves with explicitly different Weil polynomials. This exact natural-family classification is substantially more informative than a routine reduction or a point-count experiment.
